title: Inverted Index
text: Search engine storage maps each normalized term to sorted document identifiers and term frequencies. Postings lists avoid scanning every document when a user issues a keyword query.

title: BM25 Relevance Ranking
text: BM25 combines inverse document frequency, term frequency saturation, and document length normalization. Rare useful words can carry more weight than common words across a collection.

title: Search Tokenization
text: A tokenizer normalizes case, separates tokens, removes stop words, and applies light stemming. Indexing and querying must use the same analyzer to preserve retrieval correctness.

title: Variable Byte Postings Compression
text: Variable byte encoding stores integer document gaps with a small number of bytes. Delta coded postings reduce storage and help search systems load index data efficiently.

title: Query Expansion
text: Query expansion adds related terms to improve recall when searchers and documents use different vocabulary. Expansion can also decrease precision if unrelated concepts are introduced.

title: Document Frequency
text: Document frequency counts how many documents contain a term. BM25 uses corpus-wide frequency to distinguish rare technical phrases from common words.

title: Top K Retrieval
text: A top K query asks for only the highest scoring results. A heap can retain the strongest candidates without sorting all matched documents.

title: Memory Mapped Search Index
text: Memory mapping lets a process read postings from a file as needed. Operating system paging can reduce startup time and avoid loading entire indexes into Python objects.

title: Web Crawling and Robots Rules
text: A crawler discovers pages through links, respects robots instructions, and limits request rates. HTML extraction should discard navigation, scripts, and boilerplate before indexing content.

title: Index Freshness and Rebuilding
text: A prebuilt read-only index offers predictable startup and query behavior. Periodic rebuilds trade immediate freshness for simpler storage and deployment.

title: Search Precision and Recall
text: Precision describes the fraction of returned search results that are relevant. Recall describes the fraction of relevant documents retrieved. Ranking systems balance these measures.

title: Search Result Snippets
text: A search interface can show titles, ranked scores, and short explanatory snippets. Clear metadata helps readers understand why a result matched a query.

title: Consistent Hashing
text: A consistent hash ring assigns document keys to shard owners. Adding or removing a shard can move fewer keys than a modulo based partitioning scheme.

title: Scatter Gather Search
text: A coordinator sends each search request to multiple shard services in parallel. It merges ranked local responses into one global top K result set.

title: Circuit Breaker Pattern
text: A circuit breaker temporarily stops calls to an unhealthy downstream service after repeated failures. Its open, half-open, and closed states reduce repeated timeout costs.

title: Tail Latency in Distributed Systems
text: Tail latency describes the slowest requests, not average responses. Parallel fanout can amplify delays because the coordinator may wait for the slowest shard.

title: Retry With Exponential Backoff
text: Retries can recover from transient errors but may overload an already struggling dependency. Exponential backoff and jitter reduce synchronized retry storms.

title: Connect and Read Timeouts
text: A connection timeout limits network establishment time while a read timeout limits waiting for a response. Separate budgets make slow and unreachable services easier to diagnose.

title: Replication and Availability
text: Replica copies can serve requests when a node becomes unavailable. Replication adds consistency and synchronization tradeoffs that differ from partitioning documents across shards.

title: Leader Election
text: Leader election selects one participant to coordinate an operation. Distributed databases use terms, leases, or consensus protocols to avoid competing writers.

title: Load Balancing
text: A load balancer distributes requests among healthy server instances. Reverse proxies can forward traffic while adding request headers and managing connection limits.

title: Service Discovery
text: Service discovery maps logical service names to current network endpoints. In a local Docker Compose environment, container DNS allows the coordinator to find shard services.

title: Graceful Degradation
text: A distributed search service can return results from healthy shards when one shard fails. The response should explicitly mark partial coverage instead of presenting incomplete results as complete.

title: Network Partitions
text: A network partition prevents some services from communicating. Systems must choose how to handle unavailable peers and communicate whether results are stale or partial.

title: FastAPI Backend
text: FastAPI provides Python HTTP routes, request validation, and automatic OpenAPI documentation. Separate services can expose health, statistics, and search endpoints.

title: REST API Contract
text: A predictable API uses documented query parameters, status codes, and JSON responses. Input validation rejects missing or invalid search parameters before executing the query.

title: Asyncio Concurrency
text: Python asyncio runs nonblocking tasks on an event loop. It is useful for handling many slow network calls without allocating one operating system thread per request.

title: Service Metrics
text: Metrics such as request latency, error counts, and cache hit rates help operators understand performance. Percentile latency and per-shard failures reveal problems hidden by averages.

title: Health Checks and Readiness
text: A health endpoint lets hosting infrastructure identify a running process. Readiness also needs to consider dependencies before a multi-process service starts accepting traffic.

title: Docker Containers
text: Docker images bundle application code and runtime dependencies into repeatable artifacts. Containers make environment assumptions explicit through files, ports, and commands.

title: Nginx Reverse Proxy
text: Nginx can accept public HTTP traffic and forward requests to an internal coordinator. It supports proxy headers, upstream routing, and configurable connection limits.

title: Continuous Integration
text: A CI pipeline runs tests for each code change and records pass or failure status. Smoke tests should exercise the real HTTP paths in addition to unit tests.

title: Immutable Deployment Artifacts
text: An immutable container image can include a prebuilt index at build time. Restarting the container then restores the same read-only demo data without fetching a dataset.

title: Environment Variables
text: Environment variables configure service ports, index paths, and shard URLs without hardcoding them into Python modules. Secrets must not be committed to public repositories.

title: API Rate Limiting
text: Rate limiting controls how often clients can call an endpoint. It reduces resource exhaustion and abusive traffic, particularly on publicly accessible demo services.

title: Structured Application Logs
text: Structured logs include timestamps, severity, service identity, and request context. Clear log fields make debugging across coordinator and shard processes easier.

title: AI Agent Orchestration
text: An AI agent workflow coordinates language model decisions and external tools. Reliable orchestration needs explicit state, error handling, deadlines, and termination conditions.

title: Tool Calling and Validation
text: A language model can request a tool with structured arguments. A server should validate parameters, enforce permissions, and handle tool errors before returning observations.

title: Context Window Budgeting
text: A context budget divides limited model tokens among instructions, retrieved documents, conversation history, and tool output. Budget enforcement prevents context overflow.

title: Vector Similarity Search
text: Vector search retrieves items based on nearby embedding vectors rather than exact keyword overlap. It can find semantic similarity but has different costs and failure modes from BM25.

title: Hybrid Keyword and Vector Retrieval
text: Hybrid search combines lexical scores with semantic vector results. A fusion strategy can improve recall while retaining exact match behavior for important terms.

title: Text Embeddings
text: An embedding model converts text into numeric vectors that encode semantic relationships. Similarity is commonly measured with cosine similarity or dot products.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation
text: Retrieval augmented generation supplies selected documents to a language model before answer generation. Source quality, ranking, and attribution affect answer reliability.

title: Model Evaluation
text: Evaluating AI systems requires test cases, outcome criteria, and regression tracking. Tool correctness, latency, cost, and hallucination frequency all matter for production use.

title: Message Queues
text: Queues decouple producers from workers and support asynchronous jobs. Delivery guarantees, idempotency, and retry handling determine whether work is safely repeated.

title: Data Pipeline Reliability
text: Data ingestion pipelines extract, transform, and index records. Input validation, checkpointing, and reproducible builds reduce the risk of corrupt or incomplete search data.

title: Container Memory Limits
text: Small hosted containers have strict memory ceilings. Lightweight indexes, single-worker services, and avoiding unused libraries can keep a distributed demo within a free tier.

title: Render Docker Deployment
text: Render can build a Docker image from a GitHub branch and expose a public HTTPS web service. A cloud-specific Dockerfile can keep the original development stack unchanged.
